en.title: McDavid and Draisaitl visit a Carolina team that rarely loses twice
en.deck: Two of the league's best records meet in a Saturday matinee in Raleigh: Edmonton is 17-4-3 and Carolina 16-3-3. Both lost on Thursday, and the Hurricanes have not dropped two in a row since the first two games of the season. Model and market agree that Carolina is a clear favourite.
news: Connor McDavid's season-opening 23-game point streak ended in Thursday's 3-1 loss in Tampa Bay, which also ended Edmonton's six-game winning streak. He still leads the NHL with 55 points.
Taylor Hall is honoured before the game for reaching 1,000 NHL games, against the Oilers, the team that drafted him first overall in 2010.

Oilers: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins has missed three games and saw doctors on Friday. Frederik Andersen, Mattias Janmark, Alec Regula and Matt Savoie are out. Tristan Jarry or Devon Levi will start; neither is confirmed.
Carolina lists no injuries. Pyotr Kochetkov is 12-1-1 with a 1.64 GAA but has not been named the starter, and the Hurricanes play the Rangers on Sunday afternoon.
records: Leon Draisaitl leads the NHL with 21 goals.
Nikolaj Ehlers has a four-game point streak and 27 points in 33 career games against Edmonton.
Jackson Blake's 11-game point streak ended on Thursday.
Edmonton won the Oct. 22 meeting 6-5 in a shootout. The last seven meetings averaged 7.4 goals.
betting: Market: Hurricanes 1.56, Oilers 2.50, about 62–38 without the margin. The model has Carolina at 63%, right in line.
Total: over 5.5 at 1.65 is about 58% without the margin, and the model says 58% too. Over 6.5 (about 47%) also matches the model.
Player chances (model): McDavid 1+ point 76% (market about 74%), Draisaitl 1+ point 73%, Aho 1+ point 65%.

sv.title: McDavid och Draisaitl gästar ett Carolina som sällan förlorar två raka
sv.deck: Två av ligans bästa lag möts i en lördagsmatiné i Raleigh: Edmonton har 17-4-3 och Carolina 16-3-3. Båda förlorade i torsdags, och Hurricanes har inte förlorat två raka sedan säsongens två första matcher. Modellen och marknaden är eniga om att Carolina är klar favorit.
news: Connor McDavids poängsvit på 23 matcher från säsongsstarten tog slut vid torsdagens 3-1-förlust i Tampa Bay, som också bröt Edmontons sex raka segrar. Han leder ändå NHL med 55 poäng.
Taylor Hall hyllas före matchen för sina 1 000 NHL-matcher, mot Oilers som draftade honom som etta 2010.

Oilers: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins har missat tre matcher och träffade läkare i fredags. Frederik Andersen, Mattias Janmark, Alec Regula och Matt Savoie är borta. Tristan Jarry eller Devon Levi startar, ingen av dem är bekräftad.
Carolina har inga skador. Pyotr Kochetkov har 12-1-1 och 1,64 insläppta mål per match men är inte utsedd till start, och Hurricanes möter Rangers redan på söndagseftermiddagen.

Jackson Blakes poängsvit på elva matcher tog slut i torsdags.
Edmonton vann mötet den 22 oktober med 6-5 efter straffar. De sju senaste mötena hade i snitt 7,4 mål.

en.title: Chicago opens a road trip without Connor Bedard
en.deck: The Blackhawks are 6-14-2 and start a three-game trip without Connor Bedard, who hurt his right shoulder on Tuesday and may need surgery. Calgary is 10-12-1 and has alternated wins and losses over its last five. Model and market both make the Flames a modest favourite.
news: Bedard, Chicago's points leader with 18 in 15 games, will miss at least four games, including the whole trip to Calgary, Vancouver and Seattle. Anton Frondell moves up to centre the first line.

Coach Jeff Blashill may shuffle his lines after Thursday's 4-2 loss to Columbus. Jordan Greenway and Kevin Korchinski could return, and Drew Commesso could make his season debut in goal tonight or Sunday in Vancouver.
Dustin Wolf is expected to make a third straight start for Calgary after stopping 17 shots in Thursday's 4-1 loss to Minnesota. Coach Ryan Huska expects no lineup changes.
Flames: Kevin Bahl is out, and Jonathan Huberdeau is on a conditioning loan in the AHL, so he will not play tonight.
records: Chicago has allowed 4.05 goals a game, and 4.6 over its last five.
Calgary has scored only 2.2 goals a game over its last five.
Calgary won the last meeting 3-1 on Jan. 15. The last nine meetings averaged only 5.3 goals.
64% of Chicago's games have gone over 5.5 goals this season.
betting: Market: Flames 1.63, Blackhawks 2.35, about 59–41 without the margin. The model has 57–43, a touch warmer on Chicago.
Total: over 5.5 at 1.73 is about 55% without the margin, and the model agrees at 55%. The low-scoring head-to-head history points the other way.

news: Bedard, Chicagos poängetta med 18 poäng på 15 matcher, missar minst fyra matcher, däribland hela resan till Calgary, Vancouver och Seattle. Anton Frondell flyttas upp som center i förstakedjan.

Tränaren Jeff Blashill kan kasta om kedjorna efter torsdagens 2-4 mot Columbus. Jordan Greenway och Kevin Korchinski kan göra comeback, och Drew Commesso kan göra säsongsdebut i målet i kväll eller på söndag i Vancouver.

en.deck: The Sabres stopped a five-game winless run with a 6-3 win in Washington on Thursday and trail the Panthers by five points in the Atlantic. Barkov and Marchand, both out since early October with knee injuries, are close to returning, Barkov likely first. Neither is confirmed for tonight.
Neither starter is confirmed. Daily Faceoff lists Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen for Buffalo and Jacob Markstrom for Florida.
Buffalo plays in Tampa Bay on Sunday, the second half of a back-to-back.
records: Matthew Tkachuk leads Florida with 32 points, 25 of them assists.
Tage Thompson leads Buffalo with 14 goals. Sam Reinhart has 12 for Florida.
Florida lost 5-2 to Edmonton on Tuesday.
The last 12 meetings averaged 5.7 goals.

en.title: Pittsburgh without Malkin as Nashville finally comes home
en.deck: Nashville plays its first home game in two weeks after a 7-3 loss in Minnesota, its second straight defeat after a seven-game winning streak. Pittsburgh is last in the Metropolitan at 7-12-2 and is without Evgeni Malkin. The market makes the Predators a clear favourite; the model sees close to a coin flip.
news: Malkin has an upper-body injury and will miss tonight and Sunday in Dallas. His 1,425 career points tie Bryan Trottier for 19th in NHL history.
Penguins: Nick Robertson went on injured reserve Friday, Bryan Rust practised in a no-contact jersey but stays on IR, and Avery Hayes was recalled. The starting goalie is not confirmed.
Ryan O'Reilly left Nashville's practice early on Friday with no update, so his status is unclear.
Juuse Saros is expected in goal for Nashville; Justus Annunen was pulled after six goals on 20 shots in Minnesota.
records: Pittsburgh is 2-6-1 in its last nine and lost 5-2 to St. Louis on Thursday, with Rickard Rakell scoring both goals.
Steven Stamkos has 636 career goals and is fifth all-time with 249 power-play goals.
Sidney Crosby, Malkin and Kris Letang are in their 21st season together.
Pittsburgh won the Oct. 24 meeting 3-2. The last seven meetings averaged only 5.0 goals.

sv.deck: Nashville spelar sin första hemmamatch på två veckor efter 3-7 i Minnesota, andra raka förlusten efter sju raka segrar. Pittsburgh är sist i Metropolitan med 7-12-2 och saknar Jevgenij Malkin. Marknaden gör Predators till klar favorit, modellen ser nästan en slantsingling.
news: Malkin har en överkroppsskada och missar kvällens match och söndagens i Dallas. Hans 1 425 poäng i karriären är lika många som Bryan Trottier, delad 19:e plats genom tiderna.
Penguins: Nick Robertson placerades på skadelistan i fredags, Bryan Rust tränade i tröja utan kontakt men står kvar på listan, och Avery Hayes är uppkallad. Startmålvakten är inte bekräftad.
Ryan O'Reilly lämnade Nashvilles träning i förtid i fredags utan besked, så det är oklart om han spelar.
Juuse Saros väntas stå för Nashville. Justus Annunen byttes ut efter sex insläppta på 20 skott i Minnesota.

en.title: Ovechkin's longest drought follows the Capitals into Boston
en.deck: Washington has lost four straight, giving up five or more goals each time, and was outscored 23-11 in the skid. Alex Ovechkin, in what he has said is his final season, is on a 15-game goal drought, the longest of his career. Boston opens a six-game homestand, and model and market both see a near coin flip.
news: Logan Thompson was pulled on Thursday after allowing three goals on five shots in a 6-3 loss to Buffalo, his second early exit in six starts. Coach Spencer Carbery says no decision has been made on Saturday's starter.
Ovechkin set a Capitals record with his 763rd assist, passing Nicklas Backstrom, but has one goal in 20 games and is averaging a career-low 13:35 of ice time.
Capitals: Vincent Desharnais practised fully but will not play, and Rasmus Sandin is in a no-contact jersey.
Jeremy Swayman is expected to start for Boston after making 20 saves in Wednesday's 4-1 win over Detroit, which ended a three-game losing streak.
records: Ovechkin has 930 career goals, the NHL record. His previous longest drought was 14 games, in 2023.
Alex Tuch leads Washington with 13 goals and has scored in two straight. Ryan Leonard has scored in four straight.
David Pastrnak leads Boston with 28 points in 22 games. The Bruins' power play is 3-for-30 since Oct. 27.
85% of Washington's games this season have gone over 5.5 goals. The last nine meetings averaged just 4.3.

sv.deck: Washington har förlorat fyra raka, släppt in minst fem mål i varje och förlorat svackan med 11-23 i målskillnad. Aleksandr Ovetjkin, som har sagt att detta är hans sista säsong, har gått 15 matcher utan mål, den längsta torkan i karriären. Boston inleder en hemmasvit på sex matcher, och både modell och marknad ser nästan en slantsingling.
news: Logan Thompson byttes ut i torsdags efter tre insläppta på fem skott i 3-6 mot Buffalo, hans andra tidiga uttåg på sex starter. Tränaren Spencer Carbery säger att inget beslut är taget om lördagens målvakt.
Ovetjkin satte klubbrekord med sin 763:e assist och gick förbi Nicklas Bäckström, men har ett mål på 20 matcher och spelar karriärens lägsta istid, 13:35 per match.
Capitals: Vincent Desharnais tränade fullt men spelar inte, och Rasmus Sandin tränar i tröja utan kontakt.

en.title: Leafs try to stop an eight-game slide before it nears the club record
en.deck: Toronto has lost eight straight, is winless in November and blew a 3-0 lead before losing to Los Angeles in a shootout on Thursday. Three more losses would tie the franchise record of 11. Columbus snapped its own five-game skid in Chicago, and the model makes the Blue Jackets a slight favourite even though the market has Toronto ahead.
news: GM John Chayka gave coach Jim Hiller his "full support" on Nov. 16; there are no reports of a change.
Anthony Stolarz made 25 saves on Thursday and is projected to start again. Sergei Bobrovsky is 3-9-2 with an .874 save percentage. No starter is confirmed.
Kirill Marchenko, acquired from Columbus in the Matthew Knies trade, is out against his old team, as are Colton Sissons and Max Domi.
Rick Bowness returned behind the Columbus bench on Thursday after missing three games. Sean Monahan and Conor Garland are out, and Mathieu Olivier is doubtful.
records: Auston Matthews' 68th game-opening goal set a Leafs record, passing Mats Sundin.
William Nylander has 715 points and passed George Armstrong for seventh on Toronto's all-time list.
Zach Werenski has 21 points in 21 career games against Toronto. Knies had a goal and two assists on Thursday.
Toronto's games have gone over 5.5 goals 67% of the time. The last ten meetings averaged 7.1.

en.title: Hutson chases a club record after two overtime comebacks
en.deck: Both teams won in overtime on Thursday: Philadelphia came back from 5-2 down in the third period in Ottawa, and Montreal won 2-1 in Carolina on two late Lane Hutson goals. The Canadiens are 10-2-2 in their last 14 and tied with Tampa Bay for the Atlantic lead. The market makes Montreal a clearer favourite than the model does.
news: Travis Konecny had a goal and three assists in Ottawa, including the overtime winner 39 seconds in. It was the Flyers' first three-goal third-period comeback since 2021.
Dan Vladar is projected to start for Philadelphia after Joseph Woll played Thursday. Montreal has not said whether Jakub Dobes or Jacob Fowler starts.
Canadiens: Ivan Demidov, Chris Kreider, Josh Anderson, Sam Montembeault and Mike Matheson are out, and Zack Bolduc is day-to-day after missing Thursday.
Philadelphia, coached by Rick Tocchet, is 4-1-1 in its last six after an 0-6-3 start.
records: Hutson has a point on Montreal's last six goals. A point on the next one sets the club record for a defenceman, ahead of Matheson, Sheldon Souray and Chris Chelios.
The Flyers have won the last three meetings, and Konecny has 11 points in his last 11 games against Montreal.
The last nine meetings averaged 7.1 goals.

en.title: Panarin expected back as the Kings test Ottawa's point streak
en.deck: Ottawa has points in seven straight (5-0-2) even after blowing a 5-2 lead to Philadelphia on Thursday. Los Angeles has won the first two games of a five-game trip and has been far better away (5-3-2) than at home (2-8-0). The model sees a closer game than the market.
news: Artemi Panarin, the Kings' leader with 19 points, missed Thursday's game for personal reasons and is expected to return.
Adrian Kempe scored the only shootout goal in Thursday's 4-3 win in Toronto, and Darcy Kuemper made 24 saves. The Kings' starter tonight is not confirmed.
Linus Ullmark (10-1-0, .940) is likely to start for Ottawa. Samuel Ersson gave up five goals on the last seven shots he faced on Thursday.
Senators: Andre Burakovsky, Warren Foegele and William Eklund are out.
records: Tim Stützle has 277 career assists, tied with Jochen Hecht for second among German-born NHL players. His next assist moves him into second alone.
Los Angeles won the Oct. 29 meeting 6-5 in overtime on a Quinton Byfield goal, with three assists from Drew Doughty.
Ottawa's power play is converting 12.9% of its chances, last in the league.
The last seven meetings averaged 7.0 goals, but fewer than half of either team's games have gone over 5.5 this season.
betting: Market: Senators 1.57, Kings 2.48, about 61–39 without the margin. The model has 55–45, clearly warmer on Los Angeles.
Total: over 5.5 at 1.78 is about 53% without the margin. The model says 49%, a little below the market, with one of the lowest expected totals on the slate (5.8).

en.title: Cizikas set for his 1,000th game, every one of them as an Islander
en.deck: Casey Cizikas is expected to play his 1,000th NHL game and become the fourth player to reach the mark with the Islanders. New York has points in six straight (3-0-3), while Detroit is 3-9-0 since Dylan Larkin left the lineup. The market leans to the Islanders, the model slightly to the Red Wings.
news: Ryan Pulock left Thursday's 4-3 overtime loss in Winnipeg in the second period and could not put weight on his leg. Logan Stanley is also out and Alexander Romanov is on injured reserve. Pulock's status is unconfirmed.

Red Wings: Larkin has been out since Oct. 29 amid his trade request, and Simon Edvinsson is in a contract holdout. Detroit lost 4-1 in Boston on Wednesday.
John Gibson (4-7-1, .862) is Detroit's probable starter. Neither goalie is confirmed.
records: Peter DeBoer and Todd McLellan are tied for 15th in NHL coaching wins with 673. Tonight's winner takes 15th alone.
Simon Holmstrom has a career-best six-game point streak. Matthew Schaefer's 32 career goals tie Bryan Trottier's Islanders record for a teenager.
The Islanders have scored first in six straight games.
The last nine meetings averaged 5.9 goals.

en.title: Bratt's point streak meets a Blues team that is scoring again
en.deck: New Jersey is 15-7-0 and had won ten of 12 before Wednesday's 3-2 home loss to Montreal, Connor Hellebuyck's first defeat as a Devil. St. Louis has won two straight and four of five, with 13 goals in its last two games. Model and market both make the Devils the favourite, the model by less.
news: Hellebuyck is 7-1-0 since the Oct. 23 trade from Winnipeg. Joel Hofer (9-6-1, .923) is the likely St. Louis starter. Neither is confirmed.

Blues: Connor McMichael will not play and Sean Walker is likely to come in. Ross Johnston and Dillon Dube are also out. St. Louis hosts Edmonton on Sunday.
Jimmy Snuggerud and Dylan Holloway each scored twice in Thursday's 5-2 win over Pittsburgh, and Hofer made 31 saves.
records: Jesper Bratt has a nine-game point streak and is tied with Scott Niedermayer for second in assists in Devils history.
Robert Thomas had three assists on Thursday, reaching 344 and passing Alex Pietrangelo for third in Blues history.
New Jersey won the Nov. 5 meeting 5-4 in overtime on a Bratt goal.
68% of the Devils' games have gone over 5.5 goals, but the last seven meetings averaged only 5.1.
betting: Market: Devils 1.75, Blues 2.14, about 55–45 without the margin. The model has 52–48, slightly warmer on St. Louis.
Total: over 5.5 at 1.72 is about 55% without the margin. The model says 51%, below the market, in line with the low-scoring head-to-head history.

en.title: Gauthier chases the monthly goal record after his streak ends
en.deck: Cutter Gauthier's ten-game goal streak ended in Thursday's 4-0 loss in Colorado, but he already has 17 goals in November, three short of the NHL record for a calendar month. Anaheim has lost four of five, while Utah closes a five-game homestand after beating Colorado on Wednesday. Model and market both favour Utah, the model a little more.

Utah lost the first three games of the homestand, part of a six-game skid, before the 4-1 win over Colorado.
records: Gauthier scored 19 goals during the streak, which ended one game short of Teemu Selanne's franchise record. He is the first player with four hat tricks in one calendar month.
